terminal.description: The screen runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell opens in your workspace in case you want to look around.

tasks.title: Ring the bell when Ring for help is pressed
tasks.description:
Import `ringBell` from `desk.js`, and make the button with the class `ring` call it each time it is pressed. Nothing rings while the kiosk is being drawn.

The check uses a desk of its own that writes down every call. It looks at the calls made while the kiosk is drawn, then presses Ring for help twice and expects two rings.
nextSteps: Read "Handing React a function" in the lesson.
Give the Ring for help button its event prop.
Press it in the Browser panel and look for the desk's line in the console.
hints: React calls a function you give the button when it is clicked. Which prop takes it?
Event props start with `on` and are written in camel case. Their value is a function in curly braces, without brackets after its name.

tasks.title: Print the right ticket when a ticket button is pressed
tasks.description:
Each button with the class `ticket` calls `printTicket` from `desk.js` with its own kind, the words on the button, each time it is pressed. Nothing prints while the kiosk is being drawn.

The check changes `choices.js` to tickets of its own, presses the second button twice and the first once, and expects exactly those three tickets, in that order.
nextSteps: Read "Passing, not calling" in the lesson.
Give each button in the `map` a function that prints its own kind.
Reload the Browser panel: does the console print anything before you press?
hints: `printTicket` needs to know which ticket, so it cannot be handed over as it is.
Writing `printTicket(kind)` straight into the curly braces calls it while drawing. Wrap the call in a new function that React can call later.

tasks.title: Tell the desk which answer a visitor picks
tasks.description:
When a visitor picks an answer in the select with the class `answer`, call `recordAnswer` from `desk.js` with the answer they picked, as text, once for each pick.

The check changes `choices.js` to answers of its own, picks two of them one after the other, and expects `recordAnswer` to get each answer, in order.
nextSteps: Find the event a select fires when its choice changes.
In its handler, find the answer the visitor picked.
Pick two answers in the Browser panel and read the console.
hints: React hands your handler one argument that says what happened.
The event's `target` is the select itself, and a select's `value` is the option picked.

tasks.title: Write TicketButton and use it for the tickets
tasks.description:
Below `Kiosk`, write a component called `TicketButton` and export it by name. It takes two props:

- `kind`, the ticket, shown as the words of a `<button>` with the class `ticket`
- `onChoose`, a function it calls with `kind` each time the button is pressed

`TicketButton` never calls the desk itself: it only calls what it is given. Then draw the kiosk's ticket buttons with `TicketButton`, one per ticket, with `printTicket` as each one's `onChoose`.

The check draws `TicketButton` with kinds and an `onChoose` of its own and presses it twice, then presses ticket buttons on the kiosk.
nextSteps: Read "Handlers as props" in the lesson.
Write `TicketButton` below `Kiosk`, with its two props.
Call `onChoose` with the kind when the button is pressed.
Use `TicketButton` in the kiosk's `map`, and check that the tickets still print.
hints: The button should not know about the desk. It tells whoever drew it which ticket was chosen.
`onChoose` is a function from the props. Call it from a small function of the button's own, with `kind`. In the kiosk, hand `printTicket` over without calling it.
`<button className="ticket" onClick={() => onChoose(kind)}>{kind}</button>`, and in the kiosk `<TicketButton key={kind} kind={kind} onChoose={printTicket} />`.
